We need to produce a JUnit 4 test file DocumentTypeTest.java that comprehensively tests all methods in DocumentType: constructors, setPubSysKey, nodeName, outerHtmlHead (including behavior with different settings), outerHtmlTail (which does nothing), private has indirectly via behavior.

Need to import necessary classes: org.jsoup.nodes.DocumentType, org.jsoup.nodes.Document, org.jsoup.nodes.Document.OutputSettings, org.jsoup.nodes.Document.OutputSettings.Syntax.

We'll need to test:

- Constructor validation: first constructor checks not null for name, publicId, systemId via Validate.notNull, which throws IllegalArgumentException? Actually Validate.notNull throws IllegalArgumentException if null. So test that passing null triggers exception.

- The attributes are set: name, publicId, systemId, and PUB_SYS_KEY set to PUBLIC when publicId not blank. The has method determines blank via StringUtil.isBlank (null or whitespace). Provide non-blank publicId to cause PUB_SYS_KEY.

- Test deprecated constructors: they don't validate null; they set attributes directly. For second deprecated constructor with pubSysKey param, ensure that if pubSysKey is null, attribute not set; else attribute set.

- setPubSysKey: test null does nothing, non-null sets attribute.

- nodeName returns "#doctype".

- outerHtmlHead: need to test output string based on OutputSettings syntax and presence of attributes. Cases:

1. HTML syntax, no publicId and no systemId (both blank) -> should output "<!doctype>" (lowercase). Ensure name not present? If name not set? In default constructor they set name attr; but we can create DocumentType with empty name? name cannot be null but can be empty string maybe. But has(NAME) will check blank; blank leads to false, so no name in output. To get no publicId/systemId, we need to construct with empty strings for those. But Validate.notNull will accept empty string; has will treat empty as blank (StringUtil.isBlank). So output should be "<!doctype>" (lowercase). Also test that when name present, output includes name.

2. HTML syntax with publicId and systemId present -> should output "<!DOCTYPE name PUBLIC \"publicId\" \"systemId\">" (uppercase DOCTYPE). Actually code: if out.syntax() == Syntax.html && !has(PUBLIC_ID) && !has(SYSTEM_ID) then lowercase else uppercase. Since publicId present, uppercase.

3. XML syntax (Syntax.xml) also uppercase.

Test building the output via StringBuilder (Appendable). Use Document.OutputSettings out = new Document.OutputSettings(); out.syntax(Syntax.html) etc.

Also test that outerHtmlTail does nothing (does not modify accumulator). Ensure after calling tail, accumulator unchanged.

Edge cases: passing blank publicId (empty) but systemId non-blank? Then has(PUBLIC_ID) false, has(SYSTEM_ID) true, so uppercase.

Also test that PUB_SYS_KEY attribute appears only when publicId not blank; also when we setPubSysKey manually, it appears.

Implementation details: Since DocumentType extends LeafNode (which may have many methods). But we only need to use its public methods.

We need to compile test; need to import JUnit 4: org.junit.Test, org.junit.Before, org.junit.Assert.*.

Write test class DocumentTypeTest with multiple test methods.

Potential need to mock Document.OutputSettings? Actually can instantiate new Document.OutputSettings().

Edge: Document class maybe needed for OutputSettings; but OutputSettings is inner static class of Document, we can instantiate via new Document.OutputSettings().

Now produce the file with required start and end markers.

Let's craft the code.

Will include helper method buildOuterHtml(DocumentType dt, Syntax syntax) that returns string.

Also test that has private method works indirectly.

Make sure to include @Test(expected = IllegalArgumentException.class) for null validation.
